hints.title: Prime Factor Pair Counting
hints.text: Trailing zeroes in n factorial come exclusively from factors of ten, each produced by pairing one factor of two with one factor of five.

hints.title: Factor Five Dominance Invariant
hints.text: Factors of two appear far more frequently than factors of five in any factorial, meaning the count of factors of five strictly dictates the count of trailing zeroes.

hints.title: Legendre Formula Division Procedure
hints.text: Initialize count to zero. While n is at least five, divide n by five and add the quotient to count. Continue dividing until n drops below five. Return the total count.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log5 N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Computing n factorial directly overflows standard 64-bit integer registers when n exceeds 20 and takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting multiples of 5, 25, 125 via Legendre formula takes O(log5 N) time and O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain why factors of 5 govern trailing zeros and write the clean logarithmic division loop.
